about: CHAIN saga_danes_norway (Design/content/chains/saga_danes_norway.md): THE KINGS' SUMMER, 812 to 815. The saga of the Danes and the Vik: the war for the high seat after King Hemming's death. Thirteen cards. The count of the dead is told on the strand (s01); a beaten man's rune stick lies in Skane (s02); the new kings Harald and Reginfrid feast at Hleidr and name a muster for the north (s03); the chief at Skiringssal asks for a boat nobody would look at twice (s04); his daughter is set ashore on the Karmsund (s05); the Danish host lies in the fjord and the Vik swears (s06); sixteen Danes swear peace with the Franks and the kings' brother Hemming is given back (s07); the sons of Godfred come home from the Svear (s08). Four endings: the king without a kingdom is led over the flats from Ripa (end_exile, what happened); the two kings hold the kingdom because they were warned (end_kings, history changed); Godfred's sons take the high seat (end_sons, what happened); the Vik and its oath (end_vik, with a road that changes history). An afterword in 815, when the emperor's host crosses the Eider (s13). Progress is flags ch_saga_danes_norway_1 to _8; the branch flags _tally, _knows, _stick, _chest, _counsel, _karmsund, _told_raiders, _fed_host, _witness, _warned, _exiles_friend; the roads _road_harald, _road_sons, _road_vik; the end flags, the grand rewards and the two 'changed_' flags are listed in the chain page. Only s01 and one ending are needed; every other step is optional and decides what the endings offer. Cards are drawn on a call at their port in their months and years, so the waits are the real ones of 812 to 815. People: the ale-wife is the port's own (sliesthorp.gunnhild, ripa.tola); Hebbi (ahus.hebbi); Asgaut, Thorulf (hleidr.asgaut, hleidr.thorulf); Asgrim (skiringssal.asgrim); Gunnhild, Hallgrim (ogvaldsnes.gunnhild, ogvaldsnes.hallgrim); Asulf (cast.asulf); Dragomir (cast.dragomir); Horik (cast.horik). Real and only spoken of or seen: Harald, Reginfrid, their brothers Anulo and Hemming, Sigfred, Osfrid of Skane, the sons of Godfred. INVENTED, with attested name parts: Eskil (the kings' man), Styr (the beaten man), Asny (the chief's daughter). The words are in Data/writing/chain_saga_danes_norway.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text. Sources in the notes and the chain page: Annales regni Francorum 811 to 815 and 819 (facts only, in our own words; no modern translation is quoted); Chronicon Moissiacense 813; chronicle_793.json. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: Sliesthorp or Ripa, from March 812 to May 813, drawn on a call there. King Hemming died in the winter of 811 to 812; Sigfred, nephew of King Godfred, and Anulo, nephew of an older King Harald, fought for the kingdom and both fell; Anulo's side won and made his brothers Harald and Reginfrid kings; 10,940 men are said to have died (Annales regni Francorum 812; chronicle 812-winter-danish-succession-war). Where the battle was fought is not recorded. The ale-wife is the port's own (sliesthorp.gunnhild, ripa.tola). Eskil, the new kings' man, is INVENTED (As-ketil). That a new king must give feasts and so buys wine is the game's reading. Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_1 and may set _tally.

cards.note: Step 2 (optional): Ahus in Skane, from May 812 to June 813. The men who lost in 812 'could not refuse' the new kings (ARF 812); in 813 the sons of Godfred and 'not a few of the chief men of the Danes' are found to have been in exile among the Svear (ARF 813). Skane lies on the way. Osfrid of Sconaowe is real, one of the twelve who swore on the Eider in 811 (ARF 811); which side he took in 812 is NOT recorded, and the card says only that. Hebbi is ahus.hebbi, who cuts and reads runes. Styr, the beaten man, is INVENTED. That word went by rune stick is the game's reading (sticks of this kind survive from Hedeby, 9th century (?)). Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_2 and may set _knows and _stick.

cards.note: Step 3 (optional): Hleidr, the winter of 812 to 813 (November to April). The new kings keep the hall (the game's choice, with the spine and places/hleidr.json; who held Lejre in any year is NOT recorded) and name the muster: in 813 Harald and Reginfrid went with a host to Westarfolda, 'the furthest part of their kingdom to the north-west', because its princes and people would not obey (ARF 813; chronicle 813-summer-vestfold-813). Asgaut is hleidr.asgaut, Thorulf hleidr.thorulf. The kings are seen across the fire and speak through the steward. The verse is texts_793.json verse:v10_bjarkamal_gold_list, a lay set in this hall. Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_3.

In 813 Northmen raided Frisia and carried off men, women and much plunder (Chronicon Moissiacense 813, one codex under 814; chronicle 813-frisia-raid-813); whose ships they were is NOT recorded, and that a merchant's word sent them is the game's invention, offered as a temptation with a cost that lasts (flag ch_saga_danes_norway_told_raiders). cards.note: Step 6 (optional): Skiringssal, June to August 813: the summer of the Danish host (ARF 813; places/skiringssal.json era 813). The market is shut and cattle are driven inland (the game's reading of 'a host'); the chiefs swear. How the submission was made is NOT recorded: an oath on a ring at the thing heath is the custom of the north as later written (?). Eskil is the kings' man of s01. The warning is the hinge of the chain: a house that knows what Skane knows (flag _knows) may say that Godfred's sons are coming home. He may not be believed; the kings' brother at Sliesthorp (s07) is the surer ear. Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_6 and may set _fed_host, _witness, _warned.

cards.note: Step 7 (optional): Sliesthorp, June to September 813. The new kings had asked the emperor for peace and for their brother Hemming (ARF 812; chronicle 812-harald-envoys); in 813 Frankish and Saxon lords met sixteen Danish lords beyond the Elbe, peace was sworn and the brother given back, while the kings themselves were away in Westarfolda (ARF 813; chronicle 813-summer-danish-peace-813). The place of the meeting is not named. Hemming is real; that he waited for his brothers at this port is the game's choice; whether he is the Hemming, 'a most Christian leader', killed on Walcheren in 837 is uncertain (?). Asulf is cast.asulf (sliesthorp.asulf), to whom the stick of s02 is addressed. Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_7 and may set _exiles_friend or _warned.

cards.note: Step 8, the turning: Sliesthorp, Hleidr or Ripa, from September 813 to March 814. When the kings came home from the north, the sons of Godfred and not a few of the chief men of the Danes, who had been in exile among the Svear, gathered men from every side; people from all the land of the Danes went over to them, and they drove the kings out with little trouble after one battle (ARF 813; chronicle 813-autumn-godfred-sons-return). If the house's warning was heard (flag _warned) the lines tell it otherwise: the kings came home before the leaf fell, with the host whole, and the sons got no easy battle. Eskil speaks for Harald; the envoy is a man of Godfred's sons, unnamed. Three roads, one flag each; the sons' road is shut to a house that warned the kings. The danger of each is said before the choice. Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_8 and one of _road_harald, _road_sons, _road_vik.

cards.note: ENDING 1, what really happened to Harald: Ripa, from May 814 through 815, on Harald's road when no warning was heard. In 814 Harald and Reginfrid gathered men and made war on Godfred's sons again; Reginfrid and the eldest of Godfred's sons were killed; Harald, despairing of his cause, came to the emperor and put himself in his hands (ARF 814; chronicle 814-danish-war-814, 814-harald-commends). By what road he came is NOT recorded: the way over the flats from Ripa to the Frisian shore, led by a Frisian boat, is the game's. He is seen at the landing and spoken to through Eskil. Rewards: a king's friendship that the game can read in 819 and 826 (unlock_title_kings_protection, flag ch_saga_danes_norway_harald_owes), a ring the house keeps (unlock_heirloom_haralds_ring), or the second ship he cannot man (unlock_ship_norse_allround_ship). Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_end_exile and _done.

cards.note: ENDING 2, HISTORY CHANGED: Hleidr, from May 814 through 815, for a house whose warning was heard and that stood by Harald (or never met the turning). In the annals the kings came home late, to a country already risen, and were driven out after one battle (ARF 813). Here they came home before the leaf fell with the host whole; the fight of 814 is theirs, and Godfred's sons go back over the water. Reginfrid's death and the death of Godfred's eldest son in that fight are kept as recorded (ARF 814). Sets changed_danish_kings_813: no exile of Harald at the emperor's court, no Saxon and Obodrite host over the Eider in 815, no Horik on the high seat; see the chain page for what follows. The kings' guest right is real custom; a merchants' peace by a king's word is as in the oath of 873 between Louis the German and the Danish kings Sigfred and Halfdan (Annales Fuldenses 873) (?). The cost that lasts: Godfred's sons know the name (flag ch_saga_danes_norway_sons_feud). Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_end_kings and _done.

cards.note: ENDING 3, what really happened to the kingdom: Sliesthorp, from May 814 through 815, on the sons' road, or for a house that began the story and never met the turning, if no warning was heard. Godfred's sons hold the kingdom from 813; the eldest is killed in the fight of 814 (ARF 814); in 819 two of them share the rule with Harald and two are driven out (ARF 819), so there were five at least; only Horik is ever named (cast.horik: one of the kings from 813, sole king from about 827, killed 854). He speaks here as a young man; his age is the spine's guess. Dragomir (cast.dragomir), a merchant of Reric set down here by Godfred in 808 (ARF 808), is the trusted man of the factor reward. Rewards: a plot at the kings' market (unlock_plot_sliesthorp), a factor (unlock_factor_sliesthorp) with a standing among the Danes (unlock_title_danish_guest_right) on the hard road, or the freedom of the gate (unlock_charter_sliesthorp). Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_end_sons and _done.

cards.note: ENDING 4: Skiringssal, from April 814 through 815, on the road north. The oaths of 813 were sworn to two kings who by winter had no kingdom (ARF 813), and the Vik has to decide what such an oath is worth: this is the story skiringssal.two_kings of places/skiringssal.json. What Vestfold did is NOT recorded; the Danish kings kept their claim on the Vik in name (Skre; the dossier), which is the plain road here. The hard road, for a house that stood witness on the heath, CHANGES HISTORY: the thing finds that an oath to kings who are gone binds nobody, and Vestfold keeps its own landing gifts from 814 (flag changed_vestfold_free_814). If the kings were warned and hold Denmark (flag _warned), the oath stands and that road is shut. Rewards: the hall's guest right (unlock_title_norse_guest_right), no landing gift (unlock_charter_skiringssal), a fostering tie to the chief's house (unlock_kin_asgrims_house), the marks of the Karmsund (unlock_pilot_karmsund), a plot on the shore (unlock_plot_skiringssal). Sets ch_saga_danes_norway_end_vik and _done.

cards.intention: The market at Skiringssal has had no wine, salt or glass for a year and a half, and the strand is stacked with hones nobody came for. On the heath the chiefs of the Vik are asking what an oath is worth when the men it was sworn to have lost their kingdom.

cards.note: Afterword (optional): Sliesthorp, May to September 815, for a house that has ended the chain by any road but the changed one. On the emperor's order all the Saxon counts and the Obodrites under the envoy Baldric crossed the Eider into the district called Sinlendi to restore Harald, and camped on the seventh day at the shore; Godfred's sons lay with a great force and two hundred ships on an island three miles off and would not come to battle; the host laid waste the districts round about, took forty hostages and went home (ARF 815; chronicle 814-winter-elbe-thaw for the two thaws that held it back until May). It does not happen if Harald kept his kingdom (flag ch_saga_danes_norway_end_kings). The ferryman is sliesthorp.ferryman (Hallbjorn). Step payouts only.
